correctness.rationale: The theorem and exact formulas hold. At entrance, the middle m=M−1 letters are uniformly onto N=n−1 colors other than the new color, which is absent from both the middle block and the outgoing draw. Prescribing r singleton positions leaves (N−r)! S(m−r,N−r) words for each ordered choice of their distinct colors, so the count ratio is S(m−r,N−r)/S(m,N). The generating-function identity gives (N)_r/(m)_r times [τ/(exp(τ)−1)]^r times the ratio of the two zero-truncated-Poisson local masses. The numerator and denominator departures from their respective means are both bounded: they are (r+1)(a−1)−{an} and (a−1)−{an}. This corrects the incidental r(a−1)+o(1) expression in line 60; boundedness is what the span-one local limit uses. Thus the ratio tends to one, and the joint singleton probabilities tend to exp(−rτ). For the collision bound, the supremum local mass for a sum of N−1 copies is O(N^{−1/2}) by Fourier inversion, and the conditioning denominator is Θ(N^{−1/2}). The conditional second factorial moment is therefore bounded by a constant times the unconditional one, giving an O(1/n) fixed-pair collision probability. A rescue of any of the first k departing singleton colors costs at most k²/n. With neither event, survival through k is exactly absence of singletons in the first k positions. The immediate-exit formula is the r=1 singleton probability multiplied by (n−1)/n. Stationarity partitions onto time into runs, which have finite start and end almost surely by independence of disjoint windows and the positive chance of a monochromatic window. Summing over the time elapsed from the last entry gives onto mass = entrance flux × conditional mean. Their exact counts give the finite mean and their Stirling ratio tends to a(exp(τ)−1)/τ=exp(τ) by the same local limit. The finite boundary M=n=2 uses S(0,0)=1; k=0 is automatic.
